tooltip.title: Therapeutic Armamentarium
tooltip.markdown: An overview of psoriasis treatment options, organized by their mode of delivery and mechanism.

tooltip.title: Topical Therapies
tooltip.markdown: First-line for limited or mild disease (<3-5% BSA) and used as adjuncts in moderate-to-severe disease.

tooltip.title: Topical Corticosteroids
tooltip.markdown: The mainstay of topical treatment. Available in various potencies and vehicles (creams, ointments, foams, solutions).

tooltip.title: Vitamin D Analogs
tooltip.markdown: (e.g., Calcipotriene, Calcitriol) Work by inhibiting keratinocyte proliferation. Often used in combination with steroids.

tooltip.title: Other Topical Agents
tooltip.markdown: Includes topical retinoids (Tazarotene), calcineurin inhibitors (for face/flexures), and newer agents like Tapinarof (Aryl hydrocarbon receptor agonist) and Roflumilast (PDE4 inhibitor).

tooltip.title: Phototherapy
tooltip.markdown: The use of ultraviolet (UV) light to treat widespread psoriasis. A second-line option for moderate-to-severe disease.

tooltip.title: Narrowband UVB
tooltip.markdown: The most common and effective form of phototherapy, using a specific wavelength (311 nm) of UV light.

tooltip.title: PUVA
tooltip.markdown: Psoralen plus UVA light. Highly effective but less commonly used now due to increased skin cancer risk and logistical challenges.

tooltip.title: Excimer Laser
tooltip.markdown: A targeted form of UVB therapy for localized, persistent plaques.

tooltip.title: Systemic Therapies
tooltip.markdown: Oral or injectable medications for moderate-to-severe psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis that work throughout the body.

tooltip.title: Traditional Oral Systemics
tooltip.markdown:
-   **Methotrexate:** An immunomodulator effective for both skin and joints.
-   **Acitretin:** An oral retinoid, particularly useful for pustular psoriasis.
-   **Cyclosporine:** A potent immunosuppressant used for rapid control of severe flares.
-   **Apremilast:** An oral PDE4 inhibitor.

tooltip.title: Biologic Agents
tooltip.markdown: Targeted monoclonal antibodies or fusion proteins that block specific cytokines or immune cells.

tooltip.title: Oral Targeted Synthetic DMARDs
tooltip.markdown: Small molecule drugs that inhibit intracellular signaling pathways.
